title: Online vector resize protocol and client fallback guide
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: introduce a low-friction online vector resize protocol that allows changing embedding dimensionality with minimal client disruption and predictable latency/cost impact. This ticket captures the engineering plan for a negotiation-based client handshake, runtime proxy support for mixed-dimension queries, staged reindex jobs, rollout signals, and rollback behavior. Scope excludes model training; assumes new model produces vectors of the new target dimension and redirection to the new index will be controlled by rollout flags.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can query endpoints during a dimension transition without getting fatal errors; server returns clear error codes when an operation is unsupported by the client version
A migration mode supports simultaneous presence of old-dimension and new-dimension vectors for the same logical namespace with correct reranking behavior
Automated background reindex job can backfill 100k documents/hour on default infra without exceeding 15% CPU overhead on search nodes
Observability exposes per-dimension hit/miss, cross-dimension fallback rate, average rerank latency, and quality delta (recall@k) during rollout
Rollback path restores full traffic to prior index within configured SLO (10 minutes) and preserves data consistency
migration_steps: 1) Add server-side capability flag: /v1/embeddings/meta returns supported_dimensions and current_primary_dimension
2) Implement client handshake in SDKs: clients include preferred_dimensions header and tolerate fallback responses
3) Build runtime proxy that routes query vectors to appropriate index and performs cross-dimension reconciliation when needed
4) Launch background reindex worker with rate limiter and resumable checkpoints; attach progress to migration dashboard
5) Start canary: 2% traffic to new-dimension index with synthetic scoring tests and offline quality evals
6) Gradually increase traffic and monitor quality/latency; enable automatic pause if quality delta > configured threshold
7) Cutover primary dimension and deprecate old index after retention period and validation
compatibility_contract: Clients and servers will negotiate a dimension compatibility token in the response header X-Emb-Dims: primary=1536; supported=1536,1024. Clients must set X-Emb-Client-Dims on requests. If client dims != primary, server may apply one of three strategies: accept and internally pad/truncate (best-effort), route to dual-query flow (query both indexes and merge scores), or respond with 412 Precondition Failed with a migration_required error. SDKs will default to dual-query for critical reranking endpoints and best-effort for approximate similarity endpoints.
api_changes: Add /v1/embeddings/meta endpoint returning JSON with keys: primary_dimension, supported_dimensions, migration_state
Deprecate implicit single-dimension contract; new SDK versions will send X-Emb-Client-Dims header
Introduce query param ?prefer_primary=true to force primary-dimension-only path for strict clients
monitoring_and_metrics: cross_dimension_fallback_rate (percentage of requests requiring dual-query or padding)
rerank_latency_p95 and p99 broken out by dim-path (primary-only vs dual-query)
quality_delta_recall_at_10 between old/new dimension on canary traffic
performance_impact: Dual-query path will increase average token-to-response latency for reranking endpoints by an estimated 18-35ms depending on index hotness. To mitigate: enable asynchronous KV cache warmup, use adaptive batching to coalesce reconciliation queries, and provide an opt-in prefer_primary flag for latency-sensitive clients. Reindex job is throttled to keep CPU < 15% on search nodes; expected index storage overhead up to 1.9x during migration.

rollback_plan: If quality regression > threshold or latency SLOs violated for >15 minutes during ramp, toggle migration_state to PAUSED which stops new dual-query routing and sets primary_dimension back for the tenant. Reindex worker is paused and progress checkpoint persisted. Failback verification includes running a replay of canary traffic against primary-only index and sanity checks on top-k recall. Target full restoration within 10 minutes for single-region tenants.
notes: Consider a lightweight online dimension adapter that stores compact projection matrices to convert between dims for approximate merging; prototype after first canary.
We should coordinate a customer-facing deprecation notice and SDK release cadence (two SDK versions with handshake) before cutting over.
Long-term: explore index format that stores variable-length vectors with explicit dim tag to reduce storage duplication.
